clue.text: Plaintiff framing base journalist

indicators.note: framing means the plaintiff's word goes round the base like a picture frame

parts.note: a suitor is one who brings a suit in court, a plaintiff
a bed is a base or foundation, as in a flower bed or a bed of rock

explanation.surface: A litigant puts a journalist in the frame, perhaps over a defamatory story.
explanation.definitionFit: A subeditor is a newspaper journalist who checks and corrects copy before printing.

clue.text: See 11
Asian mountain dog ultimately a boxer

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word dog

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was the most famous boxer of all

explanation.surface: A breed of mountain dog from Asia turns out to be a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bengali is a person from Bengal, in the east of the Indian subcontinent, so an Asian.

clue.text: Author interfering with ambassador is less ingratiating

indicators.note: interfering with says the author's name is meddling inside the run of words that follows, buried among their letters

explanation.surface: A writer's meddling makes a diplomat less fawning.
explanation.walkthrough: A remarkably long hidden answer: twelve letters across four words, from the end of ambassaDOR through IS and LESS into INGratiating.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris Lessing was a British novelist who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2007.

clue.text: Thus custom-made also, equestrian doesn't require one

parts.note: too means also, as in 'me too'

indicators.note: doesn't require says a letter is dropped from the rider

parts.note: an equestrian is a horse rider
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A rider decides a bespoke saddle is unnecessary, so the tailor-made item goes unwanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thus' is a link word here, introducing the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods made to order are built to a customer's specification, which is what custom-made means.

clue.text: Agonising marathon laps beginning to bite where one would take a dip

definitions.text: where one would take a dip

indicators.note: laps means wraps around, so the shuffled race goes round the letter taken
agonising suggests the runners' letters are writhing in pain and shuffled
beginning to points to the first letter of bite

explanation.surface: After an agonising marathon, the first nip of cold water is where a runner bathes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romans built public baths with pools for bathing, so one is a place to have a dip.

clue.text: No stomach for bottle in small restaurant

indicators.note: the stomach is the middle of the body, so this removes the middle letters of the bottle

parts.note: a carafe is a glass bottle for wine or water

explanation.surface: Someone without the appetite for wine in a little eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafe is a small informal place serving food and drink, a modest restaurant.

clue.text: Scam posted for approval

parts.note: a con is a swindle or scam
sent means posted, as a letter

explanation.surface: A fraudulent application is sent off for sign-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Consent is permission or agreement, the same as giving approval.

clue.text: Sybarite requires some cash to host dance

indicators.note: to host means to hold within, so the cash goes round the dance

parts.note: a fiver is a five-pound note, some cash
a reel is a lively Scottish folk dance

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker needs money to throw a dance party.
explanation.definitionFit: A sybarite is devoted to luxury and pleasure, as is a free-liver who indulges freely in food and drink.

clue.text: Artist having a bash, after performing in Shakespearean role

indicators.note: after says the bash comes at the end, following the rest
in puts the performing word inside the Shakespearean role

parts.note: King Lear is the title role of Shakespeare's tragedy
on means performing, as an actor is on stage
a do is a party or bash

explanation.surface: An actor playing a Shakespeare part goes on to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The performing word sits inside the king's name, not at its edge; the party word then follows the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was the Italian Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa.

clue.text: See 19
At the outset, orphan donning shoes is buoyant

indicators.note: donning means putting on, so the letter goes inside the shoes

parts.note: flats are flat-heeled shoes

indicators.note: at the outset points to the first letter of orphan

explanation.surface: An orphan putting on shoes feels light on their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that floats is buoyant, staying on the surface of the water.

clue.text: Author is assimilating magazine covered by poet and inner self

indicators.note: covered by means wrapped inside the poet's name

parts.note: Dante Alighieri was the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

indicators.note: assimilating means taking in, so is goes round the magazine

parts.note: Elle is a fashion magazine

indicators.note: inner points to the inside letters of self, its ends removed

explanation.surface: A writer absorbing a magazine, covered by a poet and their inner self, sounds like literary introspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inner' takes the middle two letters of 'self', dropping its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Danielle Steel is an American novelist, one of the best-selling writers of romantic fiction.

clue.text: Arrogant nonsense after winning

indicators.note: after says the nonsense follows the winning word

parts.note: up means ahead or winning, as in 'two goals up'
pish is an exclamation dismissing nonsense, and so nonsense itself

explanation.surface: A haughty dismissal of the losers after victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppish is an informal British word for arrogant or self-assertive, getting above oneself.

clue.text: Common utterance from first character in passion play

indicators.note: first character in points to the opening letter of passion

parts.note: play means room or freedom to move, latitude

explanation.surface: An actor in a passion play speaking an ordinary line.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a trite remark, a commonplace that is uttered often.

clue.text: Author runs into footballer in fabled loser

indicators.note: in puts the whole lot inside the fabled loser

parts.note: in Aesop's fable the hare loses its race to the tortoise

indicators.note: into puts the runs abbreviation inside the footballer's name

parts.note: Pelé was the great Brazilian footballer
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A writer pictures a footballer running at a hare that lost a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The hare is the loser in Aesop's fable of the Hare and the Tortoise.
explanation.definitionFit: Harper Lee was the American novelist who wrote To Kill a Mockingbird.

clue.text: Right losing ten in split, likely to respond under stress

indicators.note: in puts the shortened word inside the split

parts.note: to rive is to split or tear apart

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped

parts.note: exact means right or correct
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A structure strained by a split, failing to bear ten tonnes, gives way under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' tempts as the single letter R, but here it is an adjective meaning correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Reactive means tending to react to a stimulus, so it responds when stressed.

clue.text: Oz native finding everyone in action outrageously offensive, initially

indicators.note: in puts everyone inside the action

parts.note: war is military action
all means everyone

indicators.note: initially points to the first letters of outrageously and offensive

explanation.surface: An Australian finding all-out conflict shockingly rude.
explanation.definitionFit: The wallaroo is a large kangaroo-like marsupial native to Australia, Oz for short.

clue.text: See 3
Time for a revolution has to be right under our callous leaders

indicators.note: under in a down clue means placed below, so it comes after
leaders points to the first letters of our and callous

explanation.surface: A rebel says the time is ripe for uprising, and it must be right, under our heartless rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Russian Revolution of 1917 is known as the October Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: October is the month of the Bolshevik uprising, so a time for revolution.

clue.text: Try a name to conjure with in bluff author

indicators.note: in puts the shuffled letters inside the bluff

parts.note: a bluff is a steep cliff or bank, a hill

indicators.note: to conjure with suggests the letters are magically juggled into a new order

explanation.surface: An author tries out a famous name to hide behind in a bluff.
explanation.walkthrough: A name to conjure with is an idiom for a famous name; here it signals rearranging the letters of 'Try a name'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilary Mantel was the English novelist who wrote Wolf Hall, winning two Booker Prizes.

clue.text: In days of yore, Queen's ending silence in Game of Thrones?

indicators.note: in puts the ending and the silence inside the game

parts.note: loo is an old card game, and a loo is also a throne in slang, hence the question mark

indicators.note: ending points to the last letter of Queen

parts.note: to gag someone is to silence them

explanation.surface: An old-time queen silenced in the fantasy saga Game of Thrones.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is a card game and, in British slang, a toilet, jokily called a throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Long ago means in the distant past, the days of yore.

clue.text: End with short break in Spain, getting the most out of it?

definitions.text: getting the most out of it?

parts.note: a tip is the end of something, as the tip of a finger

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a siesta is the afternoon rest taken in Spain

explanation.surface: Finishing a short Spanish holiday by making the most of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipsiest means most drunk, and a cryptic hint for being the most out of it, as one says of the inebriated.

clue.text: Believer in a single cause working in film

indicators.note: in puts the working word inside the film

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on a window
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: A one-cause fanatic working in the movies.
explanation.definitionFit: A monist holds that reality comes from a single principle or substance, a single ultimate cause.

clue.text: Artist to chew over

definitions.meaning: Edvard ... was the Norwegian painter of The Scream
to eat steadily, champing at food

explanation.surface: An artist pondering something.
explanation.definitionFit: Munch is the Norwegian painter, and to munch is to chew food steadily.

clue.text: See 24
Author in prime of life, aspire grotesquely to shroud it in darkness

indicators.note: to shroud it in means wrapping the jumbled letters inside the darkness

parts.note: murk is gloom or darkness

indicators.note: grotesquely suggests the letters are distorted into a new shape
prime of points to the first letter of life, its prime position

explanation.surface: A writer in her prime aspires grotesquely to cloak her work in gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Muriel Spark was the Scottish novelist who wrote The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie, nodded to by 'prime of life'.

clue.text: Cuckoo stealing 500 kerchiefs

indicators.note: stealing means taking in, so the crazy word goes round the number

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, cuckoo
D is the Roman numeral 500

explanation.surface: A cuckoo makes off with 500 handkerchiefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandanas are large coloured kerchiefs worn on the head or neck.

clue.text: Composer partial to rubber gloves

indicators.note: partial to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A composer who has a fondness for rubber gloves.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School, known for Wozzeck.

clue.text: Excavation in Egyptian capital with illustrations including hieroglyphs, primarily

indicators.note: capital means the capital letter at the head of the word Egyptian
including means the illustrations take in the letter

parts.note: artwork is the illustrations in a publication

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of hieroglyphs

explanation.surface: An archaeological dig in Cairo with drawings that include hieroglyphs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egyptian capital' looks like Cairo but is just the capital letter of Egyptian.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthwork is a bank or mound of earth, made by digging, an excavation.
